datasets.description: This latent fires on short-to-medium, self-contained sentences with clear subject-predicate structure, regardless of grammatical well-formedness. It responds to sentence completeness and syntactic simplicity rather than grammaticality per se, explaining its modest AUC (0.59) on the CoLA acceptability task.

top_disagreements.text: It started to rain after Jackie and me, we had finally gotten to our seats.
It started to rain after Jackie and me, we had finally gotten to our seats.
That's the most kind answer that I ever heard.
Groceries are bulging in the bag.

datasets.quality_analysis: The top latent (6858) does NOT cleanly capture grammaticality. Its AUC of 0.59 is barely above chance. It fires strongly on complete, well-formed-sounding sentences regardless of subtle grammatical errors. All 10 label disagreements are sentences labelled ungrammatical (label=0) that the latent activates highly on. Several of these are borderline acceptable in informal English — e.g. 'That's the most kind answer that I ever heard' and 'It started to rain after Jackie and me, we had finally gotten to our seats' use colloquially common constructions. This exposes a known weakness in CoLA: its expert-annotated binary labels conflate formal grammatical violations with pragmatically acceptable informal usage. The latent essentially captures 'sounds like a natural complete sentence', which disagrees with CoLA's prescriptive labels on borderline cases, suggesting annotation noise in the dataset's treatment of informal-but-communicative constructions.

datasets.description: This latent activates on enthusiastic, multi-clause conversational text characterised by exclamation marks, personal anecdotes, and an upbeat emotional tone. It captures a polished-yet-casual writing style with proper sentence-ending punctuation — a superficial stylistic signature of AI-generated text that also appears in genuinely enthusiastic human social media posts.

datasets.quality_analysis: The top latent (14407) captures a SUPERFICIAL stylistic feature rather than genuine AI authorship signal. Its AUC of 0.65 is moderate. The latent responds to enthusiastic, exclamation-heavy, multi-clause personal narratives — a style that GPT-3 frequently produces when generating casual text, but that also occurs naturally in human social media posts. All 10 disagreements are human-written tweets (label=0) with high activation, featuring @-mentions, genuine emotional reactions, and exclamation marks. The last_token_distribution further confirms a superficial confound: AI texts overwhelmingly end with proper punctuation (. ? !) while human texts frequently end with spaces or mid-word characters, indicating the model may partly rely on formatting artefacts rather than deeper stylistic differences. This reveals a dataset bias: the AI-generated samples are systematically more 'polished' in punctuation and sentence structure, creating a shortcut feature that conflates enthusiasm/formatting with AI authorship. Any classifier using this latent risks high false-positive rates on enthusiastic human writers.
